title: Renault Revives Gordini With Racy Concept

body_markdown:
Renault is on a retro-electric roll. Following the new 5, then the 4, and the insane 5 Turbo 3E, the latest car from France’s history books to be given an EV makeover is the 8 Gordini.


Like the[R17 electric restomod](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/heavenly-17-restomod-adds-to-renaults-retro-future/) , the 8 Gordini is just a concept for now, but with Renault’s recent track record, there’s a good chance the concept will reach production.


The original Renault 8 Gordini made its debut in 1964, with a rear-mounted 1.1-liter four-cylinder engine tuned to a rally-ready 95 hp, almost twice the output of the standard road car. Engineer Amédée Gordini designed a new[hemispherical](https://www.hagerty.com/media/automotive-history/hemi-chrysler-drew-dome-forged-dynasty/) cylinder head and fitted a pair of Weber twin carbs to great effect. (No wonder he was known as “the wizard.”) The 8 Gordini went on to win six European rallies, including the Tour de Corse, and was also campaigned successfully in Australia and South Africa.


The re-imagined Renault 8 Gordini is also rear-wheel-drive but, instead of a four-cylinder engine, it uses a 270-hp electric motor. That number suggests that the 8 Gordini is using a single example of the motor in the 5 Turbo 3E, which uses two. Renault certainly seems to be doing electrification right. Its line-up of EVs wins high praise for efficiency and fun, and, perhaps even more importantly, for looking lovely.


The 8 Gordini Concept is a real looker. It reinterprets the original four-door design, exaggerating its wheel arches while maintaining its trademark pointed snout and quad headlamps. It took time to get there, mind. The process began with an in-house competition during which more than 300 sketches were submitted. Two proposals were made to the modeling stage, and the one you see here was built as a full-size concept car. Finished in a Bleu de France tribute, with white racing stripes, the result is a celebration of the past, yet still fantastically futuristic.


“With \[the\] Renault 8 Gordini Concept, we wanted to spark emotion by drawing on both our heritage and modern times, bringing together the icons of yesterday and the future,” says Renault’s vice president of design, Alexandre Malval. “This exercise in style sets out to reinvent Renault 8 Gordini for the modern day. The aim of this coupé is to inspire emotion and capture the imagination of all car enthusiasts. And when I talk about emotion, I’m not talking about nostalgia, but real passion for cars.”
